title: Umbreon Rootkit Investigation
description: Investigate and analyze the compromised systems to identify and mitigate the Umbreon rootkit's presence. This scenario simulates a realistic compromise lifecycle, from initial access to rootkit persistence.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Umbreon rootkit is a Linux rootkit that targets both x86 and ARM systems. It is designed to hide its presence and provide backdoor access to the attacker. The rootkit uses various techniques to maintain persistence and evade detection. Your task is to investigate and analyze the compromised systems to identify and mitigate the rootkit's presence. This scenario will guide you through the steps of detecting and mitigating the rootkit in a realistic compromise lifecycle.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the victim host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. The victim host's IP address is `192.168.50.5`. To proceed to the next level, enter the word `start`.
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious shared library injection
levels.content: Investigate the system for any suspicious shared libraries that might be injected into the system's library path. You are looking for a file path.
levels.solution: Check the `/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/` directory for any unusual libraries.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Rootkits often inject malicious libraries into the system's library path to maintain persistence.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check the standard library directories for unusual files.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look in the `/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/` directory for files that do not belong to standard system libraries.

levels.title: Identify the malicious system-wide preload configuration
levels.content: Examine the system-wide preload configuration to detect any malicious entries that might be used to load suspicious libraries. You are looking for a file path.
levels.solution: Check the `/etc/ld.so.preload` file for any unusual entries.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malicious preload configurations can be used to load suspicious libraries at system startup.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check the standard configuration files for system-wide preload settings.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Look in the `/etc/` directory for files related to library preloading.

levels.title: Identify the hidden file or directory artifacts
levels.content: Search for any hidden files or directories that might be used by the rootkit to store configuration files, logs, or other artifacts. You are looking for a file path.
levels.solution: Look for files or directories with names starting with a dot (e.g., `.kit_`).

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Rootkits often use hidden files or directories to store configuration and other artifacts.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Search for files or directories that are not normally visible in standard directory listings.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the `find` command to search for files or directories with names starting with a dot.
